```{python}
from lets_plot import *
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier, GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, classification_report, f1_score, precision_score, recall_score
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

LetsPlot.setup_html(isolated_frame=True)
```


```{python}
# BASE_URL = "https://github.com/byuidatascience/data4dwellings/raw/master/data-raw/dwellings_ml/dwellings_ml.csv"
# OPT_URL  = "https://github.com/byuidatascience/data4dwellings/raw/master/data-raw/dwellings_neighborhoods_ml/dwellings_neighborhoods_ml.csv"
# INFO_URL = "https://github.com/byuidatascience/data4dwellings/raw/master/data-raw/dwellings_denver/dwellings_denver.csv"

# base_df = pd.read_csv(BASE_URL)
# opt_df = pd.read_csv(OPT_URL)
# info_df = pd.read_csv(INFO_URL)

BASE_CSV = "dwellings_ml.csv"
# OPT_CSV  = "dwellings_neighborhoods_ml.csv"
# INFO_CSV = "dwellings_denver.csv"

df = pd.read_csv(BASE_CSV)
# opt_df = pd.read_csv(OPT_CSV)
# info_df = pd.read_csv(INFO_CSV)
model_df = df.copy()

# Map of short column name to something more readable—copied from the data dictionary
data_dict_preparsed = \
"""
|parcel                           |character |The parcel id                                 |
|abstrprd                         |numeric   |No clue                                       |
|livearea                         |numeric   |Square footage that is liveable               |
|finbsmnt                         |numeric   |Square footage finished in the basement       |
|basement                         |numeric   |Total square footage of the basement          |
|yrbuilt                          |numeric   |Year the home was built                       |
|totunits                         |numeric   |How many dwelling units in the building       |
|stories                          |numeric   |The number of stories                         |
|nocars                           |numeric   |size of the garage in cars                    |
|numbdrm                          |numeric   |Number of bedrooms                            |
|numbaths                         |numeric   |Number of bathrooms                           |
|sprice                           |numeric   |Selling price                                 |
|deduct                           |numeric   |Deduction from the selling price              |
|netprice                         |numeric   |Net price of home                             |
|tasp                             |numeric   |Tax assesed selling price                     |
|smonth                           |numeric   |Month sold                                    |
|syear                            |numeric   |Year sold                                     |
"""

# Actually prepare the map: strip whitespace and | bars, ignore the middle column
lines_preparsed = [line.strip('|').strip() for line in data_dict_preparsed.split('\n') if line.strip()]
mapped_lines = [tuple(line.split('|')[0::2]) for line in lines_preparsed]
data_dict = dict((line[0].strip(), line[1].strip()) for line in mapped_lines)
```

## Elevator pitch
Analysis shows that homes built before 1980 can be accurately classified using features such as living area, garage type, and number of bedrooms, with our best model (Gradient Boosting) achieving over 90% accuracy. The most important predictors were living area and garage type, indicating that newer homes tend to be larger and have an attached garage. These results provide strong evidence that machine learning models can reliably distinguish between older and newer homes based on key property characteristics.

## QUESTION|TASK 1

__Create 2-3 charts that evaluate potential relationships between the home variables and `before1980`.__ Explain what you learn from the charts that could help a machine learning algorithm. 

The following charts explore the relationships between key home features and whether a house was built before 1980:

1. **Living Area by Era:** The boxplot shows that homes built in 1980 or later tend to have a larger living area compared to those built before 1980. This suggests that living area is a strong predictor for distinguishing between the two eras.

2. **Garage Capacity by Era:** The number of cars that can fit in the garage is generally higher for newer homes. Many older homes have smaller or no garages, while newer homes are more likely to have larger garages. This variable could help a machine learning model separate the classes.

3. **Bedrooms by Era:** There is a slight increase in the number of bedrooms in newer homes, but the difference is less pronounced than for living area or garage capacity. Still, it may provide some predictive value.

These patterns indicate that features like living area and garage capacity are likely to be important for a classification model, as they show clear differences between homes built before and after 1980.

```{python}
# Map before1980 to separate t/f columns
df["before1980"] = df["before1980"].astype(bool)
df["era"] = df["before1980"].map({True: "Before 1980", False: "1980 or Later"})

plot_data = df[["livearea", "nocars", "numbdrm", "era"]]

plot1 = (
    ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=as_discrete("era"), y="livearea", fill="era")) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    ggtitle("Living Area by Era") +
    xlab("Built Era") +
    ylab("Living Area (sq ft)")
)
plot2 = (
    ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=as_discrete("era"), y="nocars", fill="era")) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    ggtitle("Number of Cars by Era") +
    xlab("Built Era") +
    ylab("Garage Capacity")
)
plot3 = (
    ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=as_discrete("era"), y="numbdrm", fill="era")) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    ggtitle("Bedrooms by Era") +
    xlab("Built Era") +
    ylab("Number of Bedrooms")
)
plot1.show()
plot2.show()
plot3.show()
```


## QUESTION|TASK 2

__Build a classification model labeling houses as being built “before 1980” or “during or after 1980”.__ Your goal is to reach or exceed 90% accuracy. Explain your final model choice (algorithm, tuning parameters, etc) and describe what other models you tried.  

After trying multiple types of models, the Gradient Boosting Classifier (with n_estimators=200 and max_depth=6) achieved the highest accuracy at over 93%, outperforming both Random Forest and Logistic Regression. Gradient Boosting was chosen as the final model because it consistently provided the best balance of accuracy and generalization on the test set. Random Forest also performed well, but Gradient Boosting slightly outperformed it in accuracy, the targeted metric. Logistic Regression was less accurate (though that was expected given the complexity of the dataset), but it was included for comparison.

```{python}
# Split the data into features used to train and the target variable
X = model_df.drop(columns=["parcel", "before1980", "yrbuilt"])
y = model_df["before1980"]

# Split the dataset into training and testing sets
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, stratify=y, test_size=0.2, random_state=42)

# Train a random forest classifier
rf = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=12, random_state=42)
rf.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred = rf.predict(X_test)
rf_acc = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
# rf_rep = classification_report(y_test, y_pred, output_dict=True)

# Train a logistic regression model
lr = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42)
lr.fit(X_train, y_train)
lr_pred = lr.predict(X_test)
lr_acc = accuracy_score(y_test, lr_pred)

# Train a gradient boosting classifier
gb = GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=200, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1, random_state=42)
gb.fit(X_train, y_train)
gb_pred = gb.predict(X_test)
gb_acc = accuracy_score(y_test, gb_pred)

print(f"""Random Forest: {rf_acc}
Logistic Regression: {lr_acc}
Gradient Boosting: {gb_acc}""")
```


## QUESTION|TASK 3

__Justify your classification model by discussing the most important features selected by your model.__ This discussion should include a feature importance chart and a description of the features. 

The feature importance chart below shows which variables the Gradient Boosting model relied on most to classify homes as built before or after 1980. The most important features are:

- **Living Area:** Larger living areas are more common in newer homes, making this the top predictor.
- **Garage Type:** Newer homes tend to have attached garages, while older homes have detached garages, if any.
- **Number of Bedrooms:** There is a slight trend toward more bedrooms in newer homes.
- **Finished Basement Area:** Newer homes are more likely to have finished basements.

These features make sense intuitively, as home designs have changed over time. The model's reliance on these variables suggests it is capturing real differences between older and newer homes, supporting its validity for this classification task.

```{python}
# Feature importance for the gradient boosting model
importance_df = (
    pd.DataFrame({"Feature": X.columns, "Importance": gb.feature_importances_})
    .sort_values("Importance", ascending=False)
    .head(15)
)

# Use the data dict to map column names to less gross names
    # This doesn't apply to all the 0/1 bool columns with the same description :P
importance_df["Label"] = importance_df["Feature"].map(data_dict).fillna(importance_df["Feature"])

importance_df["Label"] = pd.Categorical(
    importance_df["Label"],
    categories=importance_df.sort_values("Importance")["Label"],
    ordered=True
)

plot = (
    ggplot(importance_df, aes(x="Label", y="Importance")) +
    geom_bar(stat="identity", fill="#4C72B0") +
    coord_flip() +
    ggtitle("Top 15 Label Importances - Gradient Boosting") +
    xlab("Label") +
    ylab("Importance Score")
)
plot.show()
```


## QUESTION|TASK 4

__Describe the quality of your classification model using 2-3 different evaluation metrics.__ You also need to explain how to interpret each of the evaluation metrics you use.  

The quality of the Gradient Boosting model can be described using several evaluation metrics:

Accuracy his measures the proportion of correct predictions out of all predictions made. Precision is the proportion of positive predictions (homes predicted as built before 1980) that are actually correct. Recall measures the proportion of actual positives (homes truly built before 1980) that the model correctly identifies. The F1 score takes precision and recall and balances both. These metrics together show that the model is not only accurate overall, but also reliable in identifying both classes, making it suitable for this classification task.

```{python}
# Evaluation metrics for the gradient boosting model
gb_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, gb_pred)
gb_precision = precision_score(y_test, gb_pred)
gb_recall = recall_score(y_test, gb_pred)
gb_f1 = f1_score(y_test, gb_pred)

print(f"""Gradient Boosted Regression:
Accuracy: {gb_accuracy}
Precision: {gb_precision}
Recall: {gb_recall}
F1 Score: {gb_f1}""")
```
